subject: Switchplay: planning session for inference migration deep-dive
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@acme-corp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Ops Team <ops@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: architecture review for inference migration

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the intro last week. We completed our internal sync and leadership asked for a technical deep-dive to align on the migration approach from our current self-hosted stack to Redwood. The goals are:
- Confirm compatibility with our feature set (KV cache, streaming, quantized models)
- Understand traffic shaping and burst behavior with reserve capacity
- Decide on a canary plan and rollback signals

Can your team run a 60–90 minute architecture review next week? Prefer mornings PST. Proposed slots: Tue 11/17 9:30–11:00, Wed 11/18 10:00–11:30, or Fri 11/20 8:30–10:00.

We have our infra and SecOps folks on standby. Also, could you share a checklist of the artifacts we should provide beforehand?

Thanks,
Alice Park
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme Corp

---
Attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: architecture review for inference migration

Hi Alice — great to hear this is moving forward. We can definitely run a focused 75-minute architecture review and come prepared with a migration checklist. Proposed attendees from Redwood: me (program lead), Marissa (solutions architect — runtime/ops), Karthik (serving runtime lead). Sean Gallagher will be on standby to scope Dedicated capacity if we need it.

All three proposed slots work for us except Fri morning; can you prioritize Tue 11/17 09:30–11:00 PST? If that doesn't work we can do Wed 11/18 10:00–11:15 and compress to 75 minutes.

I've attached a short checklist and our suggested agenda (preview):
- 10 min intros and goals
- 20 min current-state walkthrough (Acme)
- 30 min migration architecture and compatibility discussion
- 10 min rollout/canary plan and fallback policies
- 5 min next steps and action items

Please drop any pre-reads into the Drive link I included and share who from SecOps will join.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Park <alice@acme-corp.com>

Date: 2026-11-15T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: architecture review for inference migration

Thanks Hannah — apologies, leadership flagged an exec offsite on Tue and most of the platform team is blocked. Wed 11/18 at 10:00 PST works but we need to shift 30 minutes later to 10:30 to accommodate a vendor call. Could you confirm 10:30–11:45 on Wed?

Also, on the checklist: we'll prepare sample traffic profiles (QPS, percentiles), a short dump of latency-sensitive endpoints, and the current quantization/FP settings for the models. SecOps will join but wants an inventory of what logs and audit trails Redwood can provide for a SOC2-esque review.

Alice

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: architecture review for inference migration

Alice — 10:30–11:45 Wed 11/18 confirmed. I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in and a brief Miro board. Action items for Acme before the session (per your note):
- Traffic profiles (p50/p95/p99) and representative traces
- Current model quantization/config and sample model artifact sizes
- List of endpoints that require tail-latency SLAs
- Which logs SecOps wants to validate (we'll surface audit logs, access logs, and request-level metadata by default)

From Redwood side we'll share: runbook template, fallback policy examples, and an export of our typical canary signals. Attaching a runbook template (redwood-runbook-template.docx).

Agenda (final):
1) Introductions & goals (10m)
2) Acme current state + pain points (20m)
3) Redwood migration architecture + compatibility (30m)
4) Canary & rollback signals + ops runbook (20m)
5) Next steps & owners (15m)

If you want Sean to run a short cost/throughput estimate in the session, let me know; otherwise he will be on the topline.

Invite will come from my calendar shortly.

Hannah
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
